ME-2024-LD519.aiSummary: The bill would repeal Maine rules that set up a pooled market for individual and small group health plans, so those plans would no longer have to be offered through that market. It would also remove related rules for clear choice plan designs and some rate review steps tied to the pooled market. The bill would end a related reinsurance program rule for the Maine Guaranteed Access Reinsurance Association when a pooled market is operating.

ME-2024-LD500.aiSummary: The bill would require free water testing for low-income residents with private household wells, including tests for arsenic and other contaminants, plus PFAS, which are man-made chemicals. It would also direct the state to tell people about free testing and about grants for water treatment systems. The bill would make clear that homeowners whose well water is over state limits for PFAS and other listed contaminants can get those grants.

ME-2024-LD328.aiSummary: Beginning January 1, 2026, the state would pay 100% of Medicare Part B premiums under Medicare Advantage for some retired state employees and retired teachers. It would apply only if the retiree is not eligible for federally approved Medicaid services. For retired teachers, the payment would be made through the Maine Education Association benefits trust plan.

It would remove a requirement that the Department of Health and Human Services give municipal overseers access to a real-time online database used to check if someone qualifies for help. It would also update the department’s reporting rules to include more data on who gets aid, what it is used for, and local poverty and benefit use.

ME-2024-LD195.aiSummary: The bill would create a state program to certify some small businesses in farming, fishing, and wood harvesting for a tax break tied to special savings accounts. These accounts would be used only to save money for business equipment or other capital expenses, and withdrawals not used for that purpose would count as taxable income. Contributions could be made from January 1, 2026 through December 31, 2029, and each account could hold up to $250,000.

ME-2024-LD191.aiSummary: For tax years starting on or after January 1, 2025, partnerships and S corporations could choose to pay Maine income tax at the entity level. Owners and members would get a credit equal to 90% of their share of that tax, and some nonresident members could be exempt from filing a Maine return if the entity pays the tax. The bill would also let Maine adopt rules to carry out this new tax system.

ME-2024-LD140.aiSummary: The bill would raise Maine’s homestead property tax exemption for eligible homeowners. Starting with property tax years on or after April 1, 2026, the exemption would grow by $10,000 each year until it reaches $85,000, with annual inflation adjustments starting in 2033. It affects people who qualify for the homestead exemption.

ME-2024-LD1211.aiSummary: This bill would change sales tax rules for some rented equipment and vehicles. It would narrow the definition of “automobile” so some pickup trucks and vans count only if they are not used mainly to haul goods or freight. It would also change what counts as a lease or rental for property used only at the lessor’s main business location.
